content: Post-repair quality assurance and baseline reset for motor M-104 SKF6310 bearing after planned replacement. Repair completed successfully following CASE_001 bearing failure. Post-repair vibration readings taken at 15 min, 1 hour, 4 hours, and 24 hours after restart. All readings within ISO Stage 0: 1.1, 1.0, 0.9, 0.8 mm/s RMS respectively showing healthy break-in trend. Temperature stable at 37 deg C. Shaft alignment verified 0.01 mm after installation. SCADA historian baselines updated with new post-repair values. BPFO, BPFI, BSF, and FTF frequency families checked — no anomalous peaks. Gated pass at 24-hour mark. Asset returned to production. Action taken: formal QA sign-off, updated asset history, reset RUL clock in predictive model, notified OT team to update historian alarm thresholds. Lessons learned: post-repair QA at 15 min, 1 hr, 4 hr, and 24 hr intervals provides confidence in bearing seating and lubrication adequacy. Historian baseline must be updated before next anomaly detection cycle to prevent false alerts. RUL model recalibration required after any bearing replacement.
